                    ### Question
                    A 3-year-old boy was brought in by his parents for undescended testes. The physical examination showed an absence of the left testis in the scrotum. Inguinal swelling was noted on the left side and was surgically corrected. Which of the following conditions will most likely occur in the later stages of his life?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Spermatocele
opb. Torsion testis
opc. Varicocele
opd. Epididymitis
ope. Testicular cancer

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The surgical correction of undescended testis decreases the risk of testicular cancer. Inguinal swelling, when surgically corrected, reduces the risk of torsion testis and epididymitis. The absence of the left testis in the scrotum may increase the risk of spermatocele on the contralateral side. The presence of a spermatocele on ultrasonography does not directly correlate with the later development of testicular cancer.
